definition: Patient abuse is abusive or harmful behavior directed at a patient by a healthcare worker or caregiver within a care setting. In mental health services, it can arise from a mix of personal and workplace influences.

reasons: The packet supports nurse-to-patient abuse in Japanese psychiatric hospitals, but the definition generalizes to any healthcare worker or caregiver in any care setting.
“Harmful behavior” is broader than what the packet states; the source only refers to abuse.
The second sentence is only partly supported: the packet mentions individual and workplace factors, but not the broader claim that this applies generally to mental health services.
The packet only mentions nurse-to-patient abuse; it does not support extending the perpetrator to “caregiver” generally.

The packet does not explicitly define “abusive or harmful behavior” as the nature of the behavior; it refers to “abuse” without stating that it is “abusive or harmful behavior” directed at the patient.
The claim that this applies “within a care setting” is supported only insofar as the packet discusses psychiatric hospitals; it is not explicitly generalized beyond that setting in the provided text.
